Heat rejection is the transfer of collected thermal energy from the facility loop to an external sink without mixing the two fluids.
The primary cooling loop is the closed fluid path that carries heat from compute cold plates to a facility heat exchanger.
Temperature, flow, and differential-pressure sensors feed a local controller that adjusts pump speed and valve position every control interval.
Stage 1 moves coolant through cold plates where server heat enters the primary loop.

Redundant sensing reduces single-point blind spots but does not remove calibration drift risk.
A loss of reliable flow telemetry can hide a developing restriction until component temperatures begin to rise.
Shared heat-rejection saturation can affect multiple compute rows at the same time.
A combined option can address both rapid flow loss and slower sensor degradation without requiring a full plant redesign.
Facility heat-rejection capacity remains a shared upstream constraint even when the primary loop is healthy.

OPTION A
ROW 01
Option A adds pump-path redundancy and automated failover, giving the strongest interruption protection at the highest implementation effort.
OPTION B
ROW 02
Option B increases monitoring and calibration frequency, reducing detection delay at lower effort but leaving pump-path exposure unchanged.
DECISION RULE
ROW 03
Prefer an option that protects thermal margin, preserves maintainability, and can be verified through staged commissioning.
OPERATING GUARDRAIL
ROW 04
The synthetic normal supply-temperature target is 27 C with an allowed steady-state band of plus or minus 1 C.

Temperature, flow, and differential-pressure sensors feed a local controller that adjusts pump speed and valve position every control interval.
Stage 1 moves coolant through cold plates where server heat enters the primary loop.
Phase 1 records baseline alarms and flow availability; Phase 2 commissions failover under controlled load; Phase 3 audits sensor drift and operating procedures.
On a high-temperature alarm, the controller verifies sensor agreement, raises pump output, opens the standby path, and requests compute-load reduction if recovery fails.
